Travelers stop in Socaire on the way to the high-altitude lagoons. In the selected itinerary, lunch takes place here between visits to the lagoons and the onward journey to the Atacama Salt Flat.

The village adds an encounter with the settlements of the desert region to a nature-focused route. After the stop, the scenery changes again as dry plateaus give way to the salt flat.

The South Shetland Islands are known for their numerous penguin colonies, including chinstrap, Adélie, and subantarctic penguins. Seabirds nest on the coastal cliffs, while seals rest on the beaches. Whales can be seen in the surrounding waters, especially during the Southern Hemisphere summer, when marine life is particularly active.

Despite the harsh climate, the archipelago plays an important role in scientific research and polar tourism. Expedition cruises allow travelers to approach glaciers, observe colonies of marine animals, and experience the atmosphere of one of the planet's most remote regions. Weather conditions here can change rapidly, however, so shore landings and expedition routes always depend on sea conditions, wind, and ice.

A journey to the South Shetland Islands is an encounter with Antarctica in all its pristine power. Nature sets the rules here, time seems to slow down, and endless icy horizons remind visitors how remarkable and fragile our world is.

The South Shetland Islands are a gateway to Antarctica, where every iceberg, every glacier, and every encounter with wildlife becomes part of an unforgettable polar journey.
